content.text: An argument by **analogy** reasons that two things alike in some ways are alike in another way too.
What matters is relevant likeness. More relevant likenesses make the argument stronger, and relevant differences make it weaker.

examples.title: A fair analogy
lines: Mice resemble humans in the ways that matter for this drug.
examples.conclusion: So it will probably work in humans.

examples.title: A weak analogy
lines: The body is like a machine.
examples.note: The likeness has nothing to do with the conclusion.

question.prompt: What makes an argument from analogy stronger?
question.hint: Do likenesses that have nothing to do with the conclusion help?
question.explanation: Only likenesses that bear on the conclusion count. Two things both being blue does not make a drug work.
